AccessibilitySettings.description:
BL-065, 2.1.27. **POS and kiosk accessibility, which is a legal obligation in most jurisdictions and was unstated.**
**A kiosk is the hard case.** A guest with low vision using a website brings their own assistive technology; a guest at a kiosk gets whatever the kiosk offers, so the settings have to be on the device rather than in the browser.

reachableHeightModeAvailable.description: **Moves the interface to the lower half of the screen** for a guest using a wheelchair. A kiosk mounted at standing height is unusable otherwise, and no software setting fixes the mounting — this is the mitigation.

sessionTimeoutMultiplier.description: **Timeouts are an accessibility barrier nobody counts.** A guest who needs three times as long to read a screen should not lose their basket to a 90-second inactivity timer.

AppAvailability.description: **The sold-out or closed signal (decided 28 September, audit R073).** `open` is the normal state. `soldOut` shows WEB-029's sold-out state across the app while browsing still works; `closed` shows the closed state (a weather closure, a private event). Neither refuses a request on its own: it is what the guest is told, and a sale is still refused by availability where it applies. Set with `setMaintenanceMode`.

derived.description: Generated by `setAppIcons` from the source, one entry per platform and size — the iOS and Android store sets and the web favicons listed on `setAppIcons` (audit R163). Asked of Assets as renditions, an entry is pending, with no `assetRef`, until its rendition is ready (ADAM CR-106).

changeScope.description: Always `buildTime` — icons are baked into the binary.

liveVersion.description: Icon currently shipped. Differs from the draft until the next release.

requiresRebuild.description: True while the draft's source differs from the icon in `liveVersion`.

endsAt.description: Must follow `startsAt` when set (decided 28 September, audit R163). Null runs the banner with no end.

state.description: Moved by `updateBanner` between `draft` and `scheduled`, and by the schedule timer from `scheduled` to `active` and `active` to `expired` at `startsAt` and `endsAt`, in the tenant's timezone (`states/schedule.yaml`). **The rule, which no request field moves** (r8 walk of ticket 27920): a new banner is `draft`. The server sets `scheduled` when `updateBanner` leaves `startsAt` set (`endsAt` null means no end, so the banner runs until switched off; when `endsAt` is set it must follow `startsAt`), and sets `draft` again when a later update clears `startsAt`. Sending `isActive` false on an `active` banner pulls it to `draft`. `state` is derived by the server on every save and is never in a request.

BookingFlow.description: **A venue's booking flow (decided 29 September, W12: operators pick their flows, see which steps are required, set their own order).** Made from a `BookingFlowType`; lives in the working draft and reaches guests with `publishTenantConfig`, which copies the venue's flows into the version's snapshot. A product or category names its flow (catalogue `bookingFlowId`); otherwise the venue's default for the type serving its kind applies.

name.description: Staff-facing, e.g. "Day pass, date first". Not shown to guests.

isDefaultForType.description: At most one per venue and type; setting it takes it from the previous default.

isEnabled.description: A disabled flow is kept and not published; products naming it fall back to the default.

steps.description: Every step of the type, in the venue's order. Filled from the type when left out on create.

isValid.description: Whether the flow passes `validateBookingFlow`; worked out in the same transaction as each write. `publishTenantConfig` refuses a draft holding an invalid enabled flow.

scopePath.description: The partition key (ADR-0005). Written at `venue` scope.

BookingFlowConfig.description: **Set per tenant, with a per-venue override (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-11).** One tenant with several venues (the Kids Club branches, Coastal Aqua beside Union Arena) needs them to differ. The settings in force at a venue are the tenant's, with that venue's entry in `venueOverrides` laid over them field by field. The guest app resolves them for the venue the guest picked (audit R267); `effectiveForVenueId` on `getBookingFlowConfig` returns them resolved.

venueOverrides.description: Per-venue overrides, at most one per venue. A `venueId` that is not one of the tenant's active venues, or appears twice, is refused with 400. An override for a venue later closed is kept and has no effect.

BookingFlowSettings.description:
**Every guest booking-flow setting, once.** `BookingFlowConfig` is these at tenant level plus `venueOverrides`; a `BookingFlowVenueOverride` carries any subset of them for one venue (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-11). The Rev 3 settings (`timesPerPage` onwards) are the options the client's rev 3 prototype shows under Config → Booking rules and Build your experience.
**Venue-wide only (decided 29 September, W12).** The settings that belong to one flow moved to `BookingFlowLevelSettings` on each `BookingFlow`; `categoryDisplay` was removed (W7).

preset.description: L1 Ticket box … L6 Season. `auto` picks by venue type; `custom` applies none. The UI preset of the prototype's drawer (rev 3 CFG-1, no change).

cartLayout.description: `floatingIcon` is a round basket button with the item count that opens the cart (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-10). Which side a sidebar or the icon sits on in a right-to-left language is `cartSideInRtl`.

cartSideInRtl.description: **The cart side when the guest reads Arabic or another right-to-left language (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-10).** `keepRight` keeps the cart (and the floating icon) on the right, as the client confirmed; `mirror` flips it to the left with the rest of the layout.

cardLayout.description: How ticket and product cards are laid out (decided 29 September, rev 3 DG-6). Was a free string; the four values are the design's Stacked rows, Split rows, Cards across and Poster cards.

cardSize.description: Labels Compact, Standard, Large, Extra large (decided 29 September, rev 3 DG-6). `standard` replaces `regular`.

seatPicker.description: Default `bowl`, as the prototype has it (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-6). Read only for a seated event.

density.description: Labels Compact, Standard, Roomy, default Compact as the design has it (decided 29 September, rev 3 DG-6). `standard` and `roomy` replace `comfortable` and `airy`.

embedMode.description: `embedded` hides the hero banner, event page and venue header, for a flow placed inside the venue's own site.

searchInBanner.description: Off by default, as the prototype has it (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-6).

eventBannerDates.description: **Dates in event banner (decided 29 September, rev 3 23SEP-19).** On, the event banner lists the next dates; off by default. Either way the date picker sits at the top of the booking step.

timesPerPage.description: **Times per page (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-1).** When an event has more performances on the chosen day than fit, WEB-006 and GST-007 show them as compact tiles paged this many at a time with Earlier and Later; `all` shows every one. A string because `all` is one of the values.

dayPartFilter.description: **Morning, afternoon and evening chips with counts above the times (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-1).** Where each part begins is `dayPartBoundaries`.

dayPartBoundaries.description: **Where the day parts divide, in the venue's time zone (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-1).** Morning is before `afternoonStartsAt`, afternoon runs to `eveningStartsAt`, evening is from `eveningStartsAt`. A venue sets its own through `venueOverrides`. `afternoonStartsAt` must be earlier than `eveningStartsAt`, or 400.

seatViewPosition.description: **Where the view-from-your-seat box sits around the seat map (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-5).** Web only; on mobile and on a narrow screen it is always below the map.

seatTimeBar.description: **Time bar above the seat map (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-6).** Shows the chosen performance and lets the guest switch performance or change the date; switching releases the seats held for the previous one.

ticketCategories.description: **How tickets are grouped (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-16).** `categoryThenSubcategory` shows the venue's top product categories as tiles, then the tickets in the chosen one; `flatList` lists every ticket at once.

ticketTags.description: **Tags on tickets (decided 29 September, rev 3 23SEP-3).** Shows a product's display tags (such as "2 Hours", "Min 1.10 m", "Valid 90 days") on its card.

cardInfo.description: **Extra info on cards (decided 29 September, rev 3 23SEP-6).** Shows each ticket type's description, who it is for and what it includes, under its name.

conciergeMascot.description: **The concierge as mascot art or a plain button (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-5).** Read only where the `aiConciergeChat` feature is on.

showInfoOnly.description: **Show info-only products (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-14).** On, a product with `guestListing` `infoOnly` (catalogue) is listed with its not-bookable label and opens its details; off, guests are not shown it.

locationSwitcher.description: **Location switcher (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-18).** On, the booking screens carry a "Booking at" bar with Change location, reusing the guest's venue choice (audit R267). Off unless the tenant or venue enables it; it has no effect for a tenant with one venue.

guestContactFields.description: **What the guest-checkout pop-up asks, and nothing else (decided 29 September, W1).** The prototype's Email only, + name and + mobile. Must include the contact the guest's code is sent to and matched on (identity `GuestMatchPolicy.matchBy`), or 400. After the code is verified the guest is not asked for these again: the flow goes to the terms and payment, and the profile is completed later (WEB-020, GST-039). Read only where the `guestCheckout` feature is on.

dateStripDays.description: **The date strip (decided 17 September, M17-08).** How many days from today the date step shows as a strip before the calendar icon that opens the full month; later dates are picked from the calendar.

BookingFlowVenueOverride.description: **One venue's booking-flow settings where they differ from the tenant's (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-11).** `settings` carries only the fields the venue changes; a field left out inherits the tenant value, and the schema defaults do not apply inside an override.

venueId.description: One of the tenant's active venues. At most one override per venue.

BrandIdentity.description: Every `*AssetRef` here is a `MediaAsset` id from the `assets` library (`createUpload` then `completeUpload`). The image fields are PNG or SVG and at most 2 MB (decided 28 September, audit R270); `introVideoAssetRef` is a video asset within the library's limit for kind `video` (`assets.createUpload`).

logoDarkAssetRef.description: Used on dark backgrounds. Falls back to the primary logo.

logoVariant.description: **Which lockup sits in the nav bar, and whose colours drive the theme (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-4).** `light` uses `logoAssetRef`, `dark` uses `logoDarkAssetRef` (falling back to the primary logo), and `duotone` the two-colour reading of the primary logo.

faviconAssetRef.description: The browser tab icon for the guest web app.

splashImageAssetRefs.description: Splash images, shown in order. Build-time on the native apps (`splashChangeScope`); immediate on web, reaching guests with the publish (audit R163).

splashChangeScope.description: Always `buildTime` for native apps. The guest web app takes a splash change at the publish, with no build (audit R163).

introVideoAssetRef.description: **The optional intro video (decided 29 September, MOB-5).** A video `MediaAsset` from the media library (CMS-010). Streamed, so a change reaches guests with the publish and needs no app build.

introVideoMode.description: When GST-001 plays it full screen. "Skip introduction" is always shown. Anything but `off` needs `introVideoAssetRef`, or 400.

showPoweredBy.description: **"Powered by TICVAI", a configuration toggle, on by default** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q160 and the pre-apply round; consistent with DI-297; CHG-CSA-036). Shown on the launch screen and at the foot of Account and the web footer while true. **Switching it off needs the tenant's licence to allow it**: `setBrandIdentity` refuses `false` with `403 powered-by-locked` unless the tenant's plan carries the `poweredByRemoval` add-on (subscription `LicencePosition.poweredByRemovable`).

ChangeScope.description: Whether a change reaches guests on publish or needs a store release.

name.description: **Unique per tenant** (decided 28 September, audit R108). A name already used by any collection in the tenant, at any venue or level, is refused with `409 duplicate-code`.

ContentBlock.description:
BL-172. **`white-label` is excellent as a configuration model and is not an authoring surface.** `HomepageLayout` with ordered sections, `Banner`, `PromoBlock` and `ContentPage` describe what a venue has chosen; **none of them lets a marketer write something new without a developer.**
A block is a piece of authored content with a type, a body and a schedule. **The page builder is a frontend over this**, the same way the venue map's canvas is a frontend over its graph.

body.description: Typed by `kind`, and validated against the block's own schema at save. **The text a translation may fill** (R8 blocker FOUNDATION-AI-C40; the keys a body of each kind uses for its words, and the `fieldPath` a translation draft names, under `localeVariants.<locale>.`): richText `text`; image `altText`, `caption`; video `title`, `caption`; gallery `items[].altText`, `items[].caption`; cta `heading`, `text`, `label`; faq `items[].question`, `items[].answer`; form `title`, `fields[].label`, `submitLabel`; embed `title`; productGrid `heading`; countdown `heading`, `endedText`; testimonial `quote`, `author`. Every other key (links, ids, numbers, media references) is not translated.

localeVariants.description: **Per-locale bodies, not per-locale pages.** A venue running Arabic and English should not maintain two page trees that drift — the structure is shared and the words are not.

status.description: Created as `draft`; moved by `publishContentBlock` and the `publishAt`/`expireAt` timer (`states/content-block.yaml`), never by the body of a create.

publishAt.description: **Content scheduling, which the configuration model had no room for.** A seasonal banner that needs somebody awake at midnight is the same defect `Product.onSaleFrom` fixed.

audienceSegmentId.description: **Personalisation, evaluated at render.** A block shown only to members, or only to first-time visitors. Null shows it to everybody, which is what every block does today.

reviewStatus.description: The review step of `publishContentBlock`, where the tenant's publish-review policy is on (r8 walk of ticket 27919). `pending` from the 202 until the approval is decided; `status` does not change meanwhile.

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `tenant` scope.**

isEnabled.description:
BL-005. **Enablement is not publication.** A published page that is disabled exists, keeps its URL and its history, and does not render — which is what a tenant wants when a section is seasonal.
**Unpublishing loses the version; disabling does not.** Collapsing them means a venue turning off its water-park section for winter has to republish it every spring.

status.description: Created as `draft`, published by `publishTenantConfig`, archived through `updateContentPage` (`states/content.yaml`).

isReferenced.description: True when navigation or the homepage links to this page. Blocks deletion. Maintained by `setNavigation` and `setHomepageLayout` in the same transaction as the links they write.

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `tenant` scope.**

DeepLinkScheme.x-ticvai-persistence: none — derived from the primary domain and the published configuration
DeepLinkScheme.description: The URL patterns a tenant's own site uses to link into the storefront and the app (CHG-CSA-037).

baseUrl.description: The primary domain, or the platform subdomain where none is primary.

patterns.description:
**The patterns, fixed** (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-009). One per target kind, under `baseUrl`:
`product` `/p/{productId}`, `event` `/e/{eventId}`, `contentPage` `/c/{contentPageId}`, `module` `/m/{moduleKey}`,
`appSection` `/s/{appSection}`, `bookingFlow` `/book/{productId}` (optionally `?date=YYYY-MM-DD`),
`transferClaim` `/t/{transferId}?token={claimToken}` (opens `/general/ticket-transfer` in the app; ORDERS-MONEY-C12; to be confirmed before release, because a released pattern never changes). `externalUrl` and
`none` have no pattern. Campaign tags are appended as `utm_*` query parameters. A released pattern never changes: a new
target kind gets a new prefix, so a link a tenant printed keeps working. Where app links are enabled the same path opens
the app (universal links and app links on the primary domain) and the storefront where the app is not installed;
`buildDeepLink` returns the URL from these patterns and `appLink` as the same URL.

isInUse.description: True while `liveUsageCount` is above zero, that is, while live (published) content references the asset (audit R106 (10)). Drafts and collections do not count.

liveUsageCount.description: References from live (published) content only (audit R106 (10)). Expired and live is the combination that matters.

FeatureKey.description:
The feature toggles a tenant can set — one list for `FeatureToggle` and the `setFeatureToggles` body, which took a free string where the response had this enum.

**The catalogue** (`x-ticvai-feature-catalogue`; r8 walk of ticket 27776): the table below is the one source of each key's `displayName`, `changeScope` and `requiresConfiguration`. `setFeatureToggles` takes only `featureKey` and `isEnabled` from the caller; it fills the other three columns of the `whitelabel.feature_toggle` row from this table when it inserts the row, and its whole-set replace does the same for every row it writes, so no caller can set or change them. `buildTime` means a native app needs a new release to take the change, a `runtime` one takes it on the next publish. **Wallet and payment keys are `buildTime`** (stated before r8); the other values are proposals for the owner to confirm and are marked below.
| featureKey | displayName | changeScope | requiresConfiguration |
|---|---|---|---|
| digitalCompanionMode | Digital companion mode | runtime | false (proposed) |
| aiConciergeChat | AI concierge chat | runtime | true: the platform must have set an AI provider (proposed) |
| lostAndFound | Lost and found | runtime | false (proposed) |
| pushNotifications | Push notifications | buildTime | true: push credentials in the app build (proposed) |
| socialSharing | Social sharing | runtime | false (proposed) |
| multiLanguage | Multiple languages | runtime | false (proposed) |
| appleWallet | Apple Wallet passes | buildTime | true: pass certificate on the store account |
| googlePay | Google Pay | buildTime | true: payment provider setup |
| applePay | Apple Pay | buildTime | true: payment provider setup |
| cashOnDelivery | Cash on delivery | runtime | false (proposed) |
| guestCheckout | Guest checkout | runtime | false |
| uaePassLogin | UAE PASS sign-in | buildTime | true: UAE PASS client credentials (proposed) |

featureKey.description: `guestCheckout` is **off by default** (decided 17 September 2026, matrix 2.6.28, placement settled by [ADR-0045](../../docs/adr/0045-every-order-carries-a-proven-contact.md) 18 September): **the venue sets this from the configuration menu**, and it decides which routes the checkout page offers — off, the guest signs in verified at checkout; on, a guest may also check out without an account after proving their contact with a one-time code. **It gates checkout, never the cart.** The kiosk is not governed by it. Rule on `identity` `verifyGuestEmail`.

changeScope.description: Wallet and payment integrations are `buildTime` on native apps — enabling one needs a release, not a publish.

requiresConfiguration.description: True where the feature needs credentials or setup elsewhere first.

primaryArabic.description: Required when `ar` is among the tenant's languages (audit R163). A Latin face alone leaves Arabic in a system fallback that will not match.

secondaryArabic.description: Required whenever `secondaryLatin` is set and `ar` is among the tenant's languages (decided 28 September, audit R163).

changeScope.description: Custom font files are `buildTime`; selecting a bundled face is `runtime`.

FooterConfig.description:
BL-002. **`setHeader` and `HeaderConfig` exist and the footer does not**, which looked like symmetry until you notice it is not: **a header is chrome and a footer is a link surface.**
A footer carries the legal links — terms, privacy, accessibility statement, cookie preferences — and **those are the ones a regulator checks.** Treating it as a mirror of the header would have given it a logo and no way to reach a privacy notice.
**Where it is stored.** `legalLinks` and `copyrightText` are columns of `whitelabel.footer_config`; each entry of `columns` is a `whitelabel.footer_config_column` row and each entry of `socialLinks` a `whitelabel.footer_config_social_link` row. Part of the working draft (see the header). **In the tenant's own database, not the control plane (decided 28 September, audit R163)**: it moved from `control.footer_config` (renamed `whitelabel.footer_config`) and its two child tables.
**Links and order** (R8 blocker WHITE-C24 and IDENTITY-C60): a column's `links` are stored with the column, as one jsonb value in their array order; each column and each social link keeps its `sortOrder`, which `setFooter` writes from its position in the array (0 first), and every read returns `columns` and `socialLinks` ordered by it.

scopePath.description: The partition key (ADR-0005), written at `tenant` scope by the server.

sortOrder.description: The column's position, written by `setFooter` from the array order (R8 blocker IDENTITY-C60).

links.description: The column's links in display order, stored on the column row as one value (R8 blocker WHITE-C24).

legalLinks.description: **Required links, held separately from the free-form columns** — a tenant reorganising their footer must not be able to remove the privacy notice by accident.

sortOrder.description: The link's position, written by `setFooter` from the array order (R8 blocker IDENTITY-C60).

GuestListing.description: **How a product appears to a guest** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-14). `bookable`: listed and searched while it is on sale, and added to the basket. `infoOnly`: listed and searched with its details, photo and `notBookableLabel` whether or not it is on sale, and **never added to a basket** (`addCartLine` refuses it with `409`); the screen opens its details instead. `hidden`: never listed or searched for a guest, and reachable only where a staff channel sells it. Independent of `isSellable`, which says whether a channel may sell it at all.

HomepageLayout.description: **The client-approved web and app wireframes are the layout** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q163; CHG-CSA-040): sections, their order and their options follow the approved wireframes and change only where the spec breaks. **Landing-page templates** (workbook Q41 batch 2; CHG-CSA-037): a tenant with no landing page of its own starts from a TICVAI template (`templateKey`, `listLandingPageTemplates`); a tenant with its own site links into the storefront with deep links (`getDeepLinkScheme`, `buildDeepLink`).

templateKey.description: The landing-page template this layout started from (`listLandingPageTemplates`), or null for a layout composed from scratch (CHG-CSA-037).

landingSource.description: `storefront`: this home is the tenant's landing page. `ownSite`: the tenant's own website is the landing page and links in with deep links; this home is still served at the storefront address.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

**Added 20 August.** The table had no key at all — no id, no parent and no natural key, so **no row could be addressed, updated or deleted.** The response schema returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, which is the difference between an API response and a table.

maxItems.description: **How many cards the section shows, the venue's choice** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q152: every customisation option of the approved wireframe, including the card count per section; CHG-CSA-040). Replaces the fixed 1 or 2 highlights of MOB-3: the CMS offers the counts the approved wireframe offers.

scrollAnimation.description: **How the section enters as the guest scrolls** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q153: "must be there"; DI-1088; CHG-CSA-040). Rise, Scale, Slide, Blur or None, as the v4 prototype offers; `none` for guests who asked the device for reduced motion is applied whatever is set.

HomepageSectionKind.description:
**Which module each section needs, proposed, client to correct (decided 28 September, audit R163).** `tickets` needs `ticketsAndBooking`; `whatsOn` needs `events`; `attractions` needs `attractions`; `membership` needs `membership`; `dining` needs `diningAndFnb`; `shop` needs `shop`; `map` needs `map`. `heroBanner`, `quickActions`, `promotions`, `customContent`, `venueOverview` and `spacer` need no module. `venueOverview` (decided 29 September, MOB-3) is the mobile Home's description, opening hours (from `getTenantAppStatus`) and type tiles. `setHomepageLayout` refuses a visible section whose module is not enabled, and `setModuleEnablement` refuses to disable a module a section still needs.

**Which catalogue slice a type tile shows, and whose card count applies** (r8 walk of tickets 28335 and 28682; lead decision of 20 October 2026, option 1, no schema change; DEC-152 and DEC-153 stand as they are). A Home type tile is a product category, and its highlights are `listProducts(venueId, categoryId, pageSize)` in `displayOrder`, the order `listProducts` documents. The card count (`maxItems`) is that of the section whose kind matches the tile: `attractions`, `dining` or `shop`; **every other category uses the count of the `whatsOn` section**. On GST-038 (At the Venue), Food is kind `fnb` (opens GST-024), Shop is kind `retail` (GST-026), Services opens GST-029, Shows is `listPerformances` of the venue for today, and Map and Waits show in place.

**Where the Home overview, its quick actions and "Book a trip" come from in r8** (R8 blocker WHITE-C07, the lead's answer of 20 October 2026: option 3, nothing new stored). The `venueOverview` description is the published content page its section names (`contentPageId`, read with `listPublishedContentPages`); none named, the line is left out. The `quickActions` tiles are a fixed list the app shows, one per enabled module (`enabledModules` of the published configuration), in the order of the approved frame; a venue does not configure them in r8. "Book a trip" shows when the venue has a published booking flow of type `transport` (`getPublishedBookingFlow`). Configurable tiles (a section's own actions) come later, when the client asks for them.

LandingPageTemplate.description: A home page TICVAI provides for a tenant with no landing page of its own (CHG-CSA-037).

presetKey.description: The Site Builder preset it belongs to (`SiteSetupProgress.presetKey`).

languages.description: **A tenant may add or select interface languages beyond English and Arabic** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q145; CHG-CSA-039). Any ISO 639-1 language. English and Arabic ship with complete interface strings; for any other, the interface strings come as a TICVAI string pack drafted by AI translation and reviewed (T03), and a string with no translation falls back to English. Content (content pages, banners, promo blocks, FAQ entries and policies) is the tenant's to translate (`translationGaps`); product texts are Catalogue's (ADAM CR-194).

uiStringCoverage.description: How complete the interface strings are in each enabled language (CHG-CSA-039). English and Arabic are always complete; any other language is its `whitelabel.ui_string_pack` row (`UiStringPack`), or `missing` where the language has none (ADAM CR-194).

rtlLanguages.description: The enabled languages written right to left — those whose Unicode CLDR character order is `right-to-left` (Arabic, `ar`, among them). Not configured; it follows from `languages`.

translationGaps.description: Content lacking a version in an enabled language. The content is the tenant's content pages, banners, promo blocks, FAQ entries and policies; an item is missing when a `LocalisedText` of it has no value for the language (ADAM CR-194; see `setLanguages`).

areas.description: The kinds of the missing items, from the closed list `contentPages`, `banners`, `promoBlocks`, `faqs`, `policies` (ADAM CR-194). Stated here rather than as an enum, so a client built on r1, which read a free string, is not broken.

kind.description: `appSection` points at a section of the guest mobile app (decided 29 September, MOB-1), so the bottom navigation can hold Home, Explore, Plan and Tickets. `bookingFlow` (r8 walk of ticket 27905) opens the booking flow of one product, optionally on a date: `productId` is required, `date` optional; the link is `/book/{productId}?date=YYYY-MM-DD` (see `DeepLinkScheme`), and the flow shown is the one that product resolves to.

appSection.description: Required when `kind` is `appSection`. `plan` needs the `visitPlanner` module enabled, or `setNavigation` refuses it; no other value needs a module (ADAM CR-230, option A, decided 25 October 2026, which settled that only Plan maps to a module; CHG-R10TEN-003).

date.description: Used when `kind` is `bookingFlow`, the date the flow opens on. Absent opens it on today or the first date with availability, as the product page does.

LocalisedRichText.description: Keyed by language code. Values are sanitised HTML.

description.description: Set by `updateMediaAsset` and matched by `searchMedia`'s `search`. It was accepted and searched on before it had anywhere to be stored.

altText.description: Required before use in a guest-facing surface. WCAG 2.2 AA.

hasTransparency.description: Whether the image has an alpha channel with any pixel not fully opaque, recorded from the file when the upload completes; null for a file that is not an image (ADAM CR-106, option 1; CHG-R10TEN-012). White Label's setAppIcons refuses a source where it is true.

customMetadata.description:
BL-178. **`assets` is a strong contract and its metadata was fixed** — kind, title, alt text, dimensions, rights. A venue photographing four thousand products wants its own fields: shoot date, photographer, model release, season.
**Free-form and searchable, not a schema.** Every venue would want a different one, and a fixed set would be wrong for all of them.

sharedWithTenantIds.description:
BL-178. **Cross-tenant sharing, and it is refused by default for a reason.** A brand operating three venues wants one logo library; two unrelated tenants sharing an asset store is the isolation breach ADR-0011 exists to prevent.
**Only within one tenant's own scope tree.** A share naming a tenant outside it is refused rather than warned about — this is the one place where a permissive default would be a cross-tenant data leak.

categoryId.description: The asset's category, one of `MediaTaxonomy.categories[].id`; null while unclassified. Set by `bulkUpdateMediaAssets` (`setCategoryId`) (decided 29 September, data model DM4).

url.description: Signed and expiring for private assets; stable CDN URL for public ones. **A public asset that a published white-label version references is served at its stable CDN URL**, and `getPublishedTenantConfig` returns that address (`brandUrls`, `banners[].imageUrl`) so a guest client never needs this read (r8 walk of ticket 28335).

referenceCount.description: How many surfaces reference this asset. Non-zero refuses deletion.

extractedText.description: **The text pulled out of an uploaded document** (R8 blocker ORDERS-MONEY-C19): written by the upload's processing job once text extraction finishes (PDF, Word and plain-text kinds), replaced when the file is replaced, null for an image, video or audio file or while the asset is still processing. One value per asset, so AI's `ingestKnowledgeDocument` reads it through `mediaAssetRecords`.

releasedByPrincipalId.description: The reviewer who released the asset from `quarantined` (R8 blocker ORDERS-MONEY-C24, CHG-R8MIG-022); null if it never was.

derivatives.description: Generated from the original, never uploaded separately. A new breakpoint is a re-render rather than a re-upload of everything.

usage.description: Every place this asset is referenced.

affectedSurfaces.description: How many surfaces now show the new file.

liveSurfaces.description: Of those, how many are published to guests right now.

MediaRights.description: Licensing terms. Tracked because an expired licence on a live surface is a legal exposure, not a housekeeping item.

permittedTerritories.description: ISO country or region codes. **Empty means unrestricted, which is a claim rather than an absence** — an unknown territory and a worldwide licence are not the same thing, and `licenceKind: unknown` is how the second is said.

permittedChannels.description: Distribution channel codes, checked by `setMediaDistributionChannels`. Narrower than `permittedUses`, which describes the medium rather than the route.

MediaUsage.description: One place an asset is used. **`surface: product` is written by catalogue** for each item of `Product.media` (decided 29 September, rev 3 23SEP-4): `referenceId` is the product id and `isLive` is true while the product is listed to guests, which is what stops an asset in use on a ticket card being archived from under it.

extractedText.description: **Not written; read `MediaAsset.extractedText`** (R8 blocker ORDERS-MONEY-C19). Text pulled out of an uploaded document belongs to the asset, not to one place it is used, and nothing could query it here. Kept on the wire for clients built before; always absent.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

isLive.description: True where the referencing surface is published to guests.

MinimumAppVersion.description:
**The oldest guest app build still allowed to run (decided 28 September, audit R073).** A guest app whose own version is below the one for its platform shows the forced-upgrade screen (GST-047) and nothing else. Null, or a platform left null, forces nothing. Live at once through `setMaintenanceMode`, because an upgrade that must wait for a publish is not forced.

**`storeUrl`** (r8 walk of ticket 27893): the store page GST-047's "Update" button opens, one per platform, set with `setMaintenanceMode` beside the versions and live at once like them. Optional. A store address cannot be derived from `StoreAccount.appIdentifier`, which is a bundle id. The forced-upgrade screen opens the URL for the platform it runs on; where it is null the screen shows the message without the button and the guest updates from the store by hand.

storeUrl.description: The store page of the tenant's app for each platform. https only.

isLicensed.description: From the tenant's subscription. False makes enablement impossible.

referencedBy.description: Navigation items and homepage sections pointing at this module. Maintained by `setNavigation` and `setHomepageLayout` in the same transaction as the links they write. Each entry is `navigationItem:<itemId>` (written by `setNavigation`) or `homepageSection:<sectionId>` (written by `setHomepageLayout`); each operation replaces only its own entries (ADAM CR-230; CHG-R10TEN-003).

NavigationConfig.description: **The mobile tab set is venue configuration (decided 29 September, MOB-1; 29 September brief decision 6).** Before a tenant saves its own, `bottomNavigation` is Home, Explore, Plan and Tickets (each an `appSection` link), with the Buy tickets button beside them; Map is an optional tab. Plan is left out while `visitPlanner` is off.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

**Added 20 August.** The table had no key at all — no id, no parent and no natural key, so **no row could be addressed, updated or deleted.** The response schema returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, which is the difference between an API response and a table.

isVisible.description: At most five may be visible when `kind` is `bottomNavigation`; the rest overflow. The cap does not apply to `drawer` or `tabs` (ADAM CR-230).

buyButton.description: **The persistent Buy tickets button (decided 29 September, MOB-2).** On every screen of the mobile app except the booking and checkout steps; it opens GST-003. Read with `bottomNavigation`.

style.description: `raised` sits in the centre of the tab bar, as the v4 prototype shows; `hidden` turns it off.

theme.description: Deprecated with `Theme.darkMode` (CHG-CSA-035); the preview always renders the venue's theme.

outputPreviews.description: **The PDF ticket and the Apple and Google Wallet passes, previewed with the app** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q151: in Block A; CHG-CSA-041). One entry per output asked for in `outputs`.

url.description: A short-lived link to the rendered output (the PDF, the `.pkpass`, or the Google pass preview), expiring with the preview.

familyKey.description: **The same product at another location** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-18). Optional. A tenant that sells one attraction at several venues gives each venue's product the same key, e.g. `aquarium-entry`; the key names the family across the tenant and each venue has at most one product in it, so a second product at the same venue with the key is refused with `409 duplicate-code`. **What it is for:** when a guest changes location on the booking screen (the 'Booking at' switcher, `BookingFlowConfig.locationSwitcher`), lines whose product shares a `familyKey` with a product at the new venue are carried over to that product, with times and prices refreshed; every other line is cleared. Null means the product belongs to no family and its lines always clear on a switch. Compared case-insensitively, like `code`.

nameLocalised.description: **The product's name in each of the tenant's enabled languages** (6 October 2026, CHG-R4-011; the tenant's languages, not the venue's: CHG-R8PRD-009, ADAM CR-213), keyed by ISO 639-1 code, e.g. `{"en": "Aquarium entry", "ar": "دخول الأكواريوم"}`. Every guest surface shows the entry for the guest's language and falls back to `name`, which stays the name staff search and reports print. Null, or a language missing from it, means `name` is shown. At most 200 characters per language, as `name`.

descriptionLocalised.description: The product's description in each language, as `nameLocalised`; falls back to `description` (6 October 2026, CHG-R4-011).

createdByPrincipalId.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest or a visitor (R164).
createdByPrincipalId.description: 1.4.18. **The approval gate refuses an approver who is the author, and nothing recorded either.** `SeatBlock`, `DelegatedAccess` and `ManualDiscountRequest` all carry this and the product passing through approval did not.

approvedByPrincipalId.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest or a visitor (R164).

responsibleDepartmentId.description: Who owns this product commercially. A scope node at `department` level.

onSaleFrom.description: 1.4.8. **A seasonal product should not need somebody awake at midnight.** Archiving already runs on a timer in this contract, so the machinery exists; `effectiveFrom` appears on tax codes, FX rates and white-label policies and not here.

onSaleTo.description: Retires the product automatically. **Retirement is not deletion** — the product stops selling and every order that referenced it still resolves.

validTo.description: **The last moment the product's entitlements are valid; null means the same as `onSaleTo`** (ADAM CR-167 as the lead ruled it, 26 October 2026; CHG-R10OPN-003). A season pass stops selling at `onSaleTo` and is used until `validTo`: an entitlement template's `expiryAnchor` of `seasonEnd` ends here (`access#issueOrderEntitlements`). Sales closing is not validity ending.

categoryId.description: **Taken from their `fnb.product` and `retail.product`, 20 September.** `catalogue.product_category` has existed since 20 August with two operations and nothing could be filed under it — a merchandise hierarchy with a tree and no leaves. Their per-domain product tables both carried this column and ours did not.

isSellable.description:
True only when live **and** carried by a published bundle. Approval and publication are different acts.
**Derived, never set.** It changes when `transitionProductLifecycle` moves the product and when `publishBundle` carries it, so `updateProduct` does not take it — `withdraw` is how a product stops selling.

isStockTracked.description: **Taken from their `fnb.product`, 20 September.** Whether a sale decrements stock, which is not what `isSellable` asks. A ticket is sellable and tracks no stock; a bottle of water is both. Without it, an F&B sale cannot tell inventory whether to move.

segmentTags.description:
7.3.5. **A channel and a segment tag are mandatory and nothing required either.** A catalogue that cannot be filtered by segment is a catalogue nobody can report on.
**Hierarchical, not flat** — `family/with-toddlers` narrows `family` without duplicating it, which is how the promotions engine already treats scope.
**A level is a tag under `level/`** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-19): `level/beginner`, `level/intermediate`, `level/advanced`, `level/expert` (proposed codes, client to correct). A guest screen filters on it with `listProducts` `segmentTag`, and the words a guest reads beside each option come from `ProductCategory.description`, not from the tag.

codeSchema.description:
7.3.4 specifies `[ParkCode]-[ProductType]-[Variant]`. **`Product.code` existed and nothing required a format**, so a venue with three thousand products had three thousand conventions.
The tenant sets the pattern and the platform generates against it. **Validation is the point, not the string** — a code typed by hand is a code that will not sort.

entitlementTemplateId.description: What the buyer receives. Null for products that grant nothing — F&B and retail. Identity and entitlement are separate concerns.

blockedOffline.description: True for seated and retail. Seated because a seat map is not a count; retail because stock depletes in real time.

dataMaskValues.description: Custom fields. JSONB-backed, defined by the venue's data mask.

notBookableLabel.description: The label a guest reads on an `infoOnly` product, e.g. *Info only* or *Not bookable online; ask at the desk* (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-14). Each value at most 60 characters. Null means the guest screen shows its default wording. Ignored unless `guestListing` is `infoOnly`.

salesContact.description: **Who a guest contacts to book a view-only product** (decided 29 September, W3), e.g. a training course listed with full details and no Book button. Shown as *Call sales* and *Email sales* on an `infoOnly` product. Null means the venue's own contact (white-label `getTenantAppStatus.contact`). Ignored unless `guestListing` is `infoOnly`.

bookingFlowId.description: **The booking flow this product is sold through** (decided 29 September, W8 and W12): a white-label `BookingFlow` of the venue, which orders the guest's steps (for a workshop, the product first and then the date and time). Null means the category's flow (`ProductCategory.bookingFlowId`), and failing that the venue's flow for the product's `kind`. Written by `createProduct` and `updateProduct`, which refuse an id that is not a flow of the venue with `422`.

displayTags.description:
**Short facts a guest reads on the ticket card and under *Read more***: *2 Hours*, *Min 1.10 m*, *Free adult entry*, *Valid 90 days*, *Emirates ID* (decided 29 September, 23SEP-3). Not `segmentTags`, which are for reporting and segmentation and which a guest never reads.
**Derived on read when none are set.** When the venue has written no tags, a read returns tags derived from the product's duration (`clock`), entitlement validity (`calendar`) and the eligibility rule's `minHeightCm` (`height`), each marked `derived: true`; they are never stored. Once the venue writes any tag, only what it wrote is returned. Whether the guest screen shows them is `BookingFlowConfig.ticketTags` (white-label).

media.description:
**The product's own photos and video** (decided 29 September, 23SEP-4). *Read more* opens on the `isPrimary` item, and a listing shows each product's primary image, so two tickets in one category no longer share the category's picture (`ProductCategory.imageAssetId`).
Every `assetId` names an asset of the asset library (`assets.yaml` `MediaAsset`) in status `ready` whose kind matches `kind`; anything else is a `422`. **Exactly one item is `isPrimary`** when the list is not empty, and an `assetId` appears once; otherwise `400`. Setting the list records each reference as asset usage (`MediaUsage` with `surface: product`, `referenceId` the product id, `isLive` true while the product is listed to guests), which is what stops a used asset being archived from under the product.

consentQuestionIds.description: **The consent questions a guest answers when booking this product**, in the order they are asked (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-26): *Are you able to swim?*, *Do you hold a scuba certification?*, *I accept the risk*. Each id names a consent question defined in marketing-crm (`ConsentQuestion`), which owns the text, its version and whether it is asked per person or once per booking; the answer is stored there as a consent record (question version, answer, who answered, when). **One question or several, as the venue chooses.** A flow can carry its own list too (`white-label.BookingFlow.settings.consentQuestionIds`, on the product's published booking flow as `getPublishedBookingFlow` resolves it: product, then category, then the venue's flow for the kind; moved from `BookingFlowConfig` 29 September, W12); a booking asks the union of the flow's questions and those of every product in the cart, each question once (`orders.Cart.consentQuestions`). An id that names no active consent question of the tenant is a `422`.

addOnProductIds.description: **The add-ons offered with this product, in display order** (accepted 26 October 2026, Chinmay, ADAM CR-252 option A): each a `kind: addOn` product of the same venue (a coffee break, a working lunch, an AV technician offered with a meeting-room type), set in the back office. `listProducts` answers it, so WEB-048 and GST-075 read a room type's add-ons from the load they already make and fetch those products; the guest adds one as a cart line with `parentLineId`. An id that is not a `kind: addOn` product of the same venue is `400 validation` on `addOnProductIds`. Empty when none is offered.

requiresTimeWindow.description: **True for a space sold by the hour**, e.g. a meeting room type (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-13). The product is the room type (*focus pod*, *majlis*, *boardroom*, *auditorium*), never a named room; its lengths are a `length` axis (`setProductAttributes`) whose values carry `durationMinutes`, and each length is a variant priced on its own in the price list, so price is the room rate for that length. The cart line carries the booked start and end (orders), the end being the start plus the chosen variant's `durationMinutes`; `resources.listProductStartTimes` supplies the start times for a variant and a date and `allocateResources` picks the room from the product's resource requirements (`setExperienceResourceRequirements`) at checkout. True requires every active variant to have a `durationMinutes`; otherwise `422`.

productOwnerPrincipalId.description: The product owner (29 September, data model DM3), set with `setProductContextOwnership`. `responsibleDepartmentId` is the owning department.

operationalContact.description: A principal id or a name, as the context screen takes it.

brandId.description: The brand, as the context screen names it (a catalogue brand category).

eventId.description: **The event this product sells admission to** (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-011; WEB-002, WEB-004): a product page finds its event and the event's performances (`Performance.eventId`) give it dates. Null for a product not tied to an event (merchandise, a pass, a membership).

createdAt.description: **When the product was created** (ADAM CR-204, option A, decided 25 October 2026; CHG-R10CAT-007): `catalogue.product.created_at`, NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), set by the server and never by a request. Rows that predate it are backfilled by the migration task (the earliest of the product's first version's `published_at` and the migration time), then the NOT NULL and the DEFAULT are set. `listProductLifecycle` orders and filters on it.

updatedAt.description: **When the product last changed** (ADAM CR-204): set by `updateProduct` and by every product sub-resource PUT and bulk change that versions the product; null until the first change after creation. `listProductLifecycle`'s `lastModifiedAt` and `modifiedSince` read it.

ProductDisplayTag.description: One short fact on a ticket card (decided 29 September, 23SEP-3). `kind` picks the icon.

kind.description: `clock` a duration, `height` a height rule, `free` something included free, `calendar` a validity, `id` a document the guest must bring.

label.description: What the guest reads, e.g. *2 Hours*. Each language value at most 40 characters.

derived.description: True on a tag the server derived on read because the venue set none. Never sent.

ProductKind.description:
**`openDated` added 24 August** from the client's *Create Ticket Flow* board, which names six main ticket types and this was the one with no kind: **valid on any date within an eligible range, rather than for a named performance or a fixed date.**
The mechanism already existed — `access.entitlement` carries `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `entries_allowed` and `frozen_days`, which is exactly an open-dated pass. **What was missing was the product saying it is one**, so a catalogue could not offer it and a report could not count it.
**`datedAdmission` is a different thing and the two were being conflated**: dated is *this Tuesday*, open-dated is *any Tuesday between March and June*. A guest buying the second and being sold the first has bought the wrong ticket.
**Transport uses two existing kinds, not a new one** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-21). A one-way trip is `timedAdmission`: `transport.createTransportRoute` creates the route's product with one variant per passenger type, and each departure is a performance. A multi-trip or unlimited pass is `openDated`: `transport.createTransportPassType` creates it, with `EntitlementTemplate.entriesAllowed` = the pass's trips (null for unlimited), the validity = `validityDays`, and `EntitlementTemplate.transportRestriction` naming the station pair the pass was bought for, so `access` refuses it on another journey. The sale path is unchanged: both are cart lines, priced by `transport.quoteTransportFare` (orders `TransportLineAttributes`).

**`walletTopUp` added 20 October 2026** (r8 re-walk, CHG-R8RW-001): the product a wallet top-up is sold as, so the money for a top-up is taken on an order like any other sale and `createPayment` has its `orderId`. A venue has one, with one variant. Orders prices its line at the line's `quotedUnitPrice` (the amount being loaded; no tax, since stored value is a liability and not a supply), and the line may share a sale with anything else (the client-approved till's "Add top-up to sale", CHG-R8RW-009); once the order is paid, wallet `topUpWallet` credits that line's amount, once per line. A value added to a response enum, so a breaking change under ADR-0026, approved as BC-460 to BC-462; a client that does not know it shows the product as a plain product.

ProductMedia.description: One photo or video of a product, referencing the asset library (decided 29 September, 23SEP-4). One row per product and asset, so the asset library can answer which products use an asset.

isPrimary.description: The item *Read more* opens on and a listing shows. Exactly one per product.

url.description: **The asset's stable CDN address, for a guest card** (ADAM CR-221, option A, decided 25 October 2026; CHG-R10CAT-014): the asset library's public address for the asset, set on guest-facing reads (`searchCatalogue`, `listProducts` and `getProduct` for a guest or a visitor) when the asset is public and `ready`, as `getPublishedTenantConfig` returns white-label assets (`brandUrls`). Null otherwise, and on staff reads, which are unchanged. Catalogue reads the asset in process, a read the lead granted across deployables (XDR-005, 25 October 2026; CHG-R10CAT-015).

thumbnailUrl.description: The asset library's thumbnail address for the asset, on the same reads and with the same rule as `url` (ADAM CR-221).

ProductSalesContact.description: Who to contact to book a view-only product (decided 29 September, W3). At least one of `phone` or `email`.

note.description: A line shown under the contact, e.g. *Group courses are booked by phone*. At most 200 characters per language.

promotionId.description: Presentation only. A block may point at a promotion; it does not create or price one.

endsAt.description: Must follow `startsAt` when both are set (decided 28 September, audit R163).

state.description: Moved by the schedule timer at `startsAt` and `endsAt`, in the tenant's timezone, as for `Banner.state`. A new block is `draft` and moves to `scheduled` the same way as a banner: when an update leaves `startsAt` set (a null `endsAt` means no end), and back to `draft` when `startsAt` is cleared. Once `active` or `expired` the block may only be withdrawn (audit R163).

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `tenant` scope.**

translationJobId.description: The `proposeTranslations` job that drafted this proposal; `getTranslationProposals` reads a job's rows by it. Null on every other proposal (CHG-RFM-004).

targetKind.description: For a translation draft, what kind of thing it sits on (`TranslationProposals.drafts[].targetKind`); null on every other proposal (R8 blocker FOUNDATION-AI-C40).

targetRef.description: For a translation draft, the id of the block, product or template it sits on (the path id of the target's own write, e.g. a content block's `blockId`); null otherwise (R8 blocker FOUNDATION-AI-C40).

locale.description: For a translation draft, the language it is in (the job's `targetLocale`); null otherwise.

fieldPath.description: For a translation draft, where it goes inside the target, as a dotted path in the target's own body (`TranslationProposals.drafts[].fieldPath`); null otherwise. Empty for a field that is not text.

draftText.description: For a translation draft, the proposed text; null otherwise. `payload` stays the request body of the target's write, with this text at `fieldPath` (R8 blocker FOUNDATION-AI-C40).

confidence.description: For a walkway segment (`proposeWalkways`), the model's confidence in it (`WalkwayProposal.confidence`); null on every other proposal (ADAM CR-207, CHG-R10ORD-013).

basis.description: For a walkway segment, whether it was traced from a hand mark or seen in the picture (`WalkwayProposal.basis`); null otherwise (ADAM CR-207).

reasoning.description: For a walkway segment, why the model proposed it (`WalkwayProposal.reasoning`); null otherwise (ADAM CR-207).

distanceMetres.description: For a walkway segment, its length along the centreline; null where the plan has no georeference and on every other proposal (ADAM CR-207).

mapId.description: For a walkway segment, the venue map it is on (the path's `mapId`, which the target's request body does not carry); null otherwise (ADAM CR-207). `listProposedActions` filters on it.

kind.description: `content` (a marketing or storefront draft from `proposeMarketingContent`) and `audience` (a lookalike segment from `proposeLookalikeSegment`) added 29 September (build); both are applied by a person in the owning screen.

targetContract.description: Which contract would perform it. The assistant never performs it itself.

payload.description: The request body a person would submit, ready to review. **Open on purpose: its shape is the request body of `targetOperation` in `targetContract`**, and it is validated against that operation, not restated here.

status.description: **Expiry (decided 28 September, audit R213)**: a `proposed` action expires 7 days after `proposedAt`; an `approved` action not applied expires 24 hours after `decidedAt`. Both are proposed values, client to correct, and `expiresAt` carries the one that applies.

expiresAt.description: When the expiry timer moves this action to `expired` — `proposedAt` plus 7 days while `proposed`, `decidedAt` plus 24 hours once `approved`, null once `rejected`, `applied` or `expired` (audit R213).

approvalLevel.description: 8.3.65. Multi-level, because a discount and a pricing change differ in authority. **Two levels (decided 28 September, audit R213)**: `2` for anything touching prices or permissions (every `pricing` and `promotion` action, and any other whose payload sets a price, a discount, a role or a permission grant), which needs a manager other than the requester; `1` for everything else, which the requester approves themselves.

decisionReason.description: Required on rejection. **The only signal the assistant is proposing badly**, and without it a poor model degrades silently.

scopePath.description: **Added 29 September (AI design 3.1):** `ai.proposed_action` had no policy — its only references were nullable. The scope it was proposed at, and the partition key row-level security reads.

planId.description: The plan this action presents for a decision (AI design 2.2 D, 3.8).

approvalRequestId.description: The `approvals` request deciding a tier 2 or matrix-caught action (AI design 2.3).

changeSetHash.description: Hash of the change set approved; execution refuses a plan whose hash differs (AIC-181).

PublishReviewPolicy.description: Whether publishing goes through a review step (CHG-CSA-042). One row per tenant; off by default.

appliesTo.description: What the review covers. Empty means both.

scopePath.description: The partition key (ADR-0005). Written at `tenant` scope.

kind.description: The search kind of the index source the result came from (`IndexSource.kind`).

assetId.description: For kind `media`, the asset (29 September, build; 23.1.6).

matchedOn.description: Which text the match came from, so a wrong hit can be traced to a wrong tag.

SiteSetupProgress.description: **The Site Builder's saved progress, one row per tenant (decided 29 September, W12 and M24-05).** Not configuration and not published. `presetKey` is the starting point the operator picked; the builder pre-fills each step from it, which is what keeps the minimum path to a working site at about 30 minutes.

presetKey.description:
The starting point. Each preset proposes the modules, the booking flow types (with their default step order), the homepage sections, the mobile tabs and a booking-flow `preset`; nothing is written until the operator accepts a step.

**What each preset proposes** (r8 walk of tickets 27908, 27899 and 27905; lead decision of 20 October 2026, option 2). `waterPark` is DEC-159: modules `ticketsAndBooking`, `diningAndFnb`, `shop`, `map`; flows `datedDayPass` and `cabanaMap`; sections `heroBanner`, `tickets`, `attractions`, `dining`; tabs Home, Explore, Map, Tickets. **Every other preset (`themePark`, `museum`, `theatreAndArena`, `singleAttraction`, `playCentre`, `multiVenue`) proposes the same neutral default until the client supplies its own values, which then arrive as data:** flow `datedDayPass`; theme primary `#1F4E79`, secondary `#5B6770`, accent `#B85C00`, background `#FFFFFF`, text `#1A1A1A` (all pass the contrast pairs of `Theme`); header layout `logoLeft` with logo, menu and notifications shown; footer with one column, "Information", holding the policy links, and the copyright line; homepage sections and tabs from `listLandingPageTemplates` for the preset. **These values are a placeholder, not a client decision** (DI-885 awaits the client's feedback): the CMS marks them "placeholder" and must not present them as decided.

minimumPathDone.description: True once the minimum path is done: a logo, the four theme colours, at least one enabled valid booking flow and a published version. Everything else keeps its preset or schema default.

scopePath.description: The partition key (ADR-0005). Written at `tenant` scope.

SiteSetupStepKey.description: The seven Site Builder steps, in order (decided 29 September, W12): venue and modules (CMS-001), ticketing flows (CMS-103), compose steps (CMS-103), Help me choose (CMS-101), look and feel (CMS-007, CMS-009, CMS-002, CMS-004, CMS-008, CMS-005, CMS-003), mobile app (CMS-009, CMS-004, CMS-007), preview and publish (CMS-006, CMS-012, CMS-014).

TenantAppStatus.description: Computed on read. The published fields come from the current `ConfigVersion`, the maintenance fields from the tenant's `tenant_config` row (`setMaintenanceMode`), and the draft fields from the working draft. **Fields marked staff only are left out of a response to a caller without a staff session** (`getTenantAppStatus`).

isPublished.description: True once any version has been published.

darkAppModules.description: **The app-modules switched off for this tenant** (ADAM CR-164, option A, 18 October 2026; CHG-CRA-005): their keys (for example `AM-MARKETING-CRM-P01`), from the tenant's release flags. Returned to guests and staff alike; the apps leave those modules' screens out of navigation (the map is `handoff/release-flags.json`). An operation is dark for the tenant only when every app-module that binds it is off, so an operation shared with a live module stays callable. A flag the configuration does not declare counts as on. Additive: nothing new shows on screen.

hasUnpublishedChanges.description: Staff only. The working draft differs from the current version's `snapshot`.

activePageCount.description: Staff only. Content pages that are `published` and enabled.

availabilityMessage.description: What the sold-out or closed screen says (WEB-029). Null shows the default wording.

venues.description: **Public: the venues a guest can pick** (decided 28 September, audit R267; schema named 29 September, readiness close-out, our build plan). The source of the venue picker on WEB-001 and GST-001, returned with or without a session. **Published only**: a venue is listed when its scope node is active (`tenancy.OrgUnit.isActive`) and it is in the tenant's current published `ConfigVersion`; a venue added or reactivated since the last publish appears after the next publish, and a draft never reaches a guest. Ordered by `name`. Empty when nothing is published.

venueId.description: **The venue's scope node** (`tenancy.OrgUnit.id`, level venue): what every guest screen that declares `venueId` `from: session` reads once the guest picks it.

contact.description: The venue's own contact (address, phone, email), from the venue's settings (`tenancy.VenueSettings`, read through `venueSettingsRecords`). Null when the venue has none set; the app then shows the tenant's `contact` (R8 blocker WHITE-C16).

city.description: Shown under the name so two venues with similar names can be told apart.

openingHoursToday.description: Today's opening hours in the venue's time zone, from `tenancy.VenueSettings` opening hours. Null when the venue is closed today or has none set.

whatsNew.description: **Public: the guest "what's new"** (decided 29 September, rev 3 GAP-B2). Newest first, at most 10, from `platform-ops.Release.guestReleaseNotes` of the releases the tenant's cell has received; a release with no guest notes is skipped. Returned with or without a staff session.

publishedAt.description: When the release reached the tenant's cell.

recentChanges.description: Staff only. Names the principal behind each change, so it never reaches a public response.

TenantConfig.description:
**The tenant's working draft**, one row per tenant (see the header). Published versions are `ConfigVersion.snapshot`, not further rows here.
**Only `tenantId` and `version` are required**, because the draft is built one part at a time: the first `set*` call creates the row with that part alone. A part that is still unset is what `validateTenantConfig` reports (`missingRequiredAsset` and the like) and what blocks `publishTenantConfig` — a storage rule that every part exist would stop the first save.

version.description: The draft's working version label; the published one is `ConfigVersion.version`. A draft created by the first `set*` call has the version `draft` (ADAM CR-230; CHG-R10TEN-003).

isDraft.description: True for the working draft, which is the only row.

bookingFlows.description: Every venue's booking flows in the draft (`whitelabel.booking_flow`), so a publish snapshots them with the rest (decided 29 September, W12).

notificationBranding.description:
BL-003. **`marketing-crm` holds the templates and nothing said whose identity they wear.** A message sent on behalf of a venue carries that venue's sender name, reply-to and logo — **an operational alert arriving from `noreply@ticvai.com` is one a guest marks as spam.**
Resolved on the template at send time rather than duplicated per template.

enabledPaymentMethods.description: BL-004. **`FeatureToggle` could turn Apple Pay on and could not say which cards a tenant accepts.** Resolved against `orders.PaymentProvider.supportedMethods` — the tenant's choice within what the gateway offers, and **a tenant enabling a method their provider does not support should fail here rather than at checkout.**

maintenanceMessage.description: The message on the branded maintenance screen.

venues.description: The tenant's active venues, for the guest venue picker on WEB-001 and GST-001 (decided 28 September, audit R267). Public: returned without a session and cached with the rest of the response. Read from `tenancy` venues; a closed or archived venue is left out.

openingHours.description: Today's hours as shown to a guest, e.g. "10:00 to 22:00".

darkMode.description: **Deprecated and ignored** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q150 and the pre-apply round; CHG-CSA-035). White label has no dark or light mode: the venue's chosen theme is applied, on every device setting. The field is kept so a client built at r1 still parses, is accepted on `setTheme` and returned as stored, and **is never used to render anything or drawn on any screen**; the guest app has no Light/Dark switch.

cornerRadius.description: The prototype's 0 to 22 px slider sits inside these bounds (rev 3 CFG-2, no change). Its named palettes, font pairs and background tones are presets over the colours here and `FontConfig`, not stored values.

surfaceStyle.description: Cards and panels as frosted glass or opaque (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-3).

componentColours.description: **Colours for single interactive elements (decided 17 September, M17-11).** Each is optional and falls back to the theme colours. Every pair passes the same contrast check as the theme (`ContrastProblem`), or `setTheme` refuses it with 400. The guest flow stays the standard one; only the colours change.

TicketProof.x-ticvai-persistence: none — rendered on request, nothing is stored
TicketProof.description: A sample ticket from a template, **marked as a proof on the artefact itself** so it cannot be presented at a gate.

contentRef.description: Where the rendered proof can be fetched or sent to the printer from.

walletPlatform.description: Which wallet the pass preview is for, where `mediaType` is `walletPass` (DEC-151; CHG-CSP-038).

UpdateContentPageRequest.x-ticvai-persistence: none — request only; the fields land on whitelabel.content_page
UpdateContentPageRequest.description: The body of `updateContentPage`: the fields a tenant edits. `id`, `isReferenced` and `scopePath` are the server's, and `status` moves only to `archived` here — publishing is `publishTenantConfig` (`states/content.yaml`).

status.description: Only `archived` is taken — send it to withdraw a published page or abandon a draft (`states/content.yaml`). Any other value is a 400 `validation`. Omit to leave the status as it is.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

uploadUrl.description: Signed. PUT the file here, then confirm with `/complete`.

assetId.description: The asset this upload became — created by `completeUpload`, or the asset whose file `replaceMediaAsset` swapped. Null while the transfer is outstanding.

VenueContact.description: How a guest reaches the venue: WEB-028 Contact & Venue Information, and the screen shown on an error or when the app cannot help (decided 28 September, audit R073). Public, because nothing here is personal.

openingHours.description: Prose, as the guest reads it. The bookable hours are the catalogue's.
